author: Cabanis, 1851
status: 겨울철새 수만 마리 · 나그네새 수천 마리
summary: 우리나라 전역에 찾아오는 겨울새로, 못가와 습지, 갈대밭, 풀밭에서 지낸다. 시베리아에서 번식하고 한국, 만주, 중국 남부, 일본 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: pale brown lores and eye surround

sexes.male: 겨울깃은 머리와 목덜미, 등이 황갈색으로 보이고, 폭넓은 뺨선과 허리, 배는 황백색이다.
sexes.female: 수컷보다 색이 연하며, 갈색 머리에 흰 눈썹선과 뺨선이 있다.

young: 어린새는 암컷과 비슷하나 가슴과 옆구리에 갈색 세로줄이 뚜렷해, 아랫면에 줄무늬가 거의 없는 어른새와 구별된다. 이 줄무늬가 가을까지 남은 개체도 있다.

similar.how: 북방검은머리쑥새는 더 작고 부리가 가늘며 윗부리 선이 곧고, 작은날개덮깃이 잿빛(검은머리쑥새는 적갈색)이며 아랫면에 줄무늬가 거의 없다.

art.subject: Pallas's Reed Bunting (Emberiza pallasi), adult male in winter plumage, as seen in Korean reed beds from November to March: head, nape and mantle pale sandy buff-brown, the crown finely streaked; lores and the area around the eye pale brown; a broad buffy-white submoustachial stripe and a thin dark malar stripe; back with bold black streaks; lesser coverts blue-grey; two pale wing-bars; rump and uppertail coverts unstreaked buffy-white; underparts buffy-white with almost no streaks, the flanks faintly washed buff; tail dark with white outer feathers. Small bill with a straight culmen, pinkish-grey with a darker upper mandible; dark eye; pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: perched on a reed stem, side view
art.scene: Korean winter: dry reed bed at the edge of a pond with grassy margins; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male winter, side view perched on a reed stem: pale buff-brown head and back with black streaks, broad buffy-white submoustachial stripe, pale brown lores and eye surround, blue-grey lesser coverts, unstreaked buffy-white rump and belly, small straight-edged bill
adult female, side view perched: brown head with a whitish supercilium and white submoustachial stripe, streaked brown back, paler and plainer than the male
art.build: Small, slim reed bunting, about the size of a sparrow, smaller and paler than Common Reed Bunting, with a rather long, notched tail. Rounded head without a crest. Bill small and pointed with a straight upper edge, not swollen. Legs pinkish-brown. Clings to reed stems and hops on the ground below them; the white outer tail feathers show when it flies.
avoid: Do not paint rufous-brown lesser coverts, a streaked grey-brown rump or a deep, bulging bill; those mark Common Reed Bunting (Emberiza schoeniclus).
Do not give the winter male a black head; the black hood is breeding plumage only.
Do not streak the breast and flanks heavily; this species is almost plain below.
